notes.decision: Translated 'the likeness of the word.' Per terminology guide, ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ MUST be 'likeness' consistently. ⲡⲥⲉⲭⲉ = Lyc 'word, speech' (cf. accumulated ⲥⲉⲭⲉ). Chapter title introducing exegesis of the relation between the spoken word and its underlying likeness/semblance.
Translated 'the begetting.' Lyc action-noun: ⲧ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲭⲧⲟ on ⲭⲧⲟ = ϫⲡⲟ 'beget' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲭⲧⲟ 'the begetting'). Names the act of producing/uttering the word from the mouth.

Translated 'the exchange.' Likely Lyc. variant of ϣⲱⲃⲉ/ⲧϣⲱⲃⲉ 'exchange, change' or alternatively related to ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer/response.' In context (the parable of speech as coin and currency), 'exchange' fits both registers — vocal exchange between speakers and the monetary exchange that follows.

Translated as 'teeth … lips.' ⲛⲉⲭⲉ likely Lyc. variant for ⲛⲁϫϩⲉ 'teeth' (with ⲭ for ϫ); the form differs from ⲛⲁⲃⲍⲉ in the King-of-Darkness body-schema (different scribal register). ⲛⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩ likely Lyc. variant of ⲛ̄ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'their lips' (cf. ⲥⲟⲁⲡⲉⲧ in glossary). The mouth-organ chain (tongue → teeth → lips) fits the speech-production sequence.

Translated 'the body of the blank' (i.e., the unstamped metal flan). The compound likely combines ⲙⲉϣ- (a measure/weight stem, possibly cognate with ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ or ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄) with ⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'body' — yielding the unstruck metal body that gets stamped. Confidence low; alternative readings include 'the ingot,' 'the half-body,' or 'the median piece.'

ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲍϥ̄ rendered 'engraves it forth' from a stem ⲟⲩⲱⲧϩ̄/ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲍ̄ 'inscribe, mark.' The reduplicated ⲭⲉⲍⲭⲱⲍϥ̄ rendered 'engraves it' (reduplicated intensive of a ϫϩⲱϫ/ⲭⲱⲍ stem 'engrave, sharpen, stamp'). Both verbs occupy the metalwork register of coin-fashioning.

Translated 'serve as currency.' Greek χρῆμα 'thing, money, currency' verbalized with ⲛϥ-ⲣ̄-ⲟⲩ- 'and-it-shall-do/be a-.' The verbalization captures the function: the minted coin serves as monetary medium among men.
